parties:
Abul Hossain and others ------ Petitioners 
vs 
Habibullah Mia & ors ------ Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: The revisional application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the judgment and decree dated 20-5-2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 9-7-2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka, dismissing the suit.

2. The petitioners as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 116 of 1993 against the defendants for declaration of title and for permanent injunction in respect of 0.62 acres of land in plot No. 36 within mouza Mandail under Keranigonj Police Station.

3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit land was owned by Zaminder Kalinarayan Roy, who awarded Sikkim taluk of the land to his son Babu Dakhinacharan Roy; that one Haji Gandu Kha Bepari, son of Paltan Kha took possession of the Sikkim taluk and transferred the possessory right of the land in favour of his two sons Abdul Khaleque and Abdul Alek, that Haji Gandhu Kha Bepari excavated pond on the suit plot No. 36 in the year of 1320 and was in possession of the pond and he also cultivated fish and used the water of the pond. It is further stated that the residential house of Gandhu Kha Bepari was just beside the suit pond in plot No. 34; that Gandhu Kha Bepari left behind his two sons Abdul Khaleque and Abdul Alek and 5 daughters and that the land of the pond was taken in the names of his two sons and his other heirs did not receive any inheritance in the property.

4. Their further case is that Haji Mia Kha was the brother of Haji Gandhu Kha who was the eldest person in his family and started looking after all the properties of the family; that CS record accordingly, was collusively prepared in the name of Haji Mia Kha alone but still Abdul Khaleque and Abdul Alek remained in possession of the suit land and that Haji Mia Kha never claimed any independent title in the suit pond. It is further stated that Abdul Khaleque died in the year 1968 leaving behind one son Abdul Mannan, plaintiff No. 8, and 3(three) daughters namely, plaintiffs Nos. 9 to 11. Alek died in the year 1948 leaving behind son Hanif, predecessor of defendants Nos. 1 to 8, son Abul Hossain, plaintiff No. 1, son Motiur Rahman plaintiff No. 2 and son Shahabuddin, predecessors of plaintiff Nos. 4 to 7 and daughter Afia Khatoon, plaintiff No. 3 and that subsequently, during SA operation, the suit pond was wrongly recorded in the names of the defendants Nos. 9 and 10, Abdul Majid Kha and Monnaf Kha, sons, Mariam Bibi who was daughter of Haji Gandu Kha Bepari and in the name of Abdul Rashid Kha, father of defendants Nos. 11 and 12 but they did not enjoy the suit pond during the life-time of Hanif, that Hanif on their behalf possessed the suit pond. That all the rent receipts and documents were under the possession of Md Hanif and that Md Hanif during his lifetime did not claim the independent title or possession in the suit pond till his death in 1989.

5. Plaintiff's further case is that on 1-1-1993 the defendant-respondent-opposite party Nos. 1 to 3 claimed the independent title in the suit pond on the basis of purchase of the same by their father Md Hanif and restrained the plaintiffs from using the water of the pond and claimed the yearly sale proceed of the fish. Then defendant Nos. 1 to 8 disclosed that SA Khatian and mutation were exclusively prepared in the name of their father Md Hanif. On enquiry it was revealed that said mutation case was a forged one; that the defendant had no independent title and possession in the suit pond. On the other hand, the defendant Nos. 9 to 12 acquired title in the suit pond by virtue of adverse possession. Aa the defendant Nos. 1 to 8 claimed independent title in the suit pond and also restrained the plaintiffs from enjoying usufruct of the pond, hence plaintiffs are constrained to file the suit.

6. Defendant Nos. 1 to 3 contested the suit by filing a written statement alleging, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable, that the payment of the court fee is not proper and that there is no cause of action of the suit. It is further stated that the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit pond; that Haji Gandu Kha and Haji Mia Kha were not brothers as their fathers are different, and that Haji Mia Kha was the son of Pagan Bepari and Gandhu Kha was the son of Haji Ashrafuddin. Defendants' further contention is that CS record was correctly prepared in the name of Haji Mia Kha and that on the death of Haji Mia Kha, his heirs executed and registered solenama on 27-8-1916 and according to the terms of solenama the suit pond fell into the saham of his son Md Yasin Khan; that Yasin Khan left Abdul Mazid Kha, Abdul. Mannaf Kha, Abdur Rashid Kha and two daughters Kamrunnessa and Amirunnessa and a wife Mariam Bibi, that other heirs died leaving sons and daughters who acquired the permanent marashi title under the sikim taluk of Abdul Khaleque and Abdul Alek; that all the interests were extinguished after the acquisition of Zamindari system and SA record was prepared correctly in the name of Abdul Mazid and Abdul Mannaf, son of Yasin Kha, Nazir Ahmed Kha and Abdul Hamid, sons of Abdul Rashid in equal share. It is further stated that the father of the defendant Nos. 1 to 8 Md Hanif purchased the suit pond on 29-5-1973 by registered deed No. 13424 from Abdul Mannaf Khan, Nazir Ahmed Khan and Abdul Hamid Khan and later on 16-4-1980 purchased also the share of Abdul Majid Kha through registered deed No. 8112 dated 16-4-1980 and that the defendants Nos. 1 to 8 have been possessing the suit pond by paying the rents in the name of their father Md Hanif Miah who mutated his name in SA khatian. It is further stated that plaintiff brought the suit on false claims upon the suit pond as they never possessed the suit pond nor did they acquire title in suit pond, that Gandhu Kha had no title in the suit pond and thus the plaintiffs received nothing from him. Hence the suit is liable to be dismissed.

7. The plaintiffs adduced 5 witnesses and defendant adduced 5 witnesses and both the parties exhibited some documents in the trial Court in support of their respective claim.

8. The learned Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka, on consideration of the evidence on record, dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 9-7-2000 holding, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable as they brought the suit having no power on behalf of other plaintiffs and that the plaintiffs have no title and possession in the suit pond.

9. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 9-7-2002, the plaintiffs filed title appeal in the Court of the learned District Judge, Dhaka and on transfer the appeal was ultimately heard by the learned Additional District Judge, in charge of 5th Court, Dhaka, who by his judgment and decree dated 20-5-2002 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree dated 9-7-2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge in Title Suit No. 116 of 1993.

10. The point for determination is, whether the learned. Additional District Judge committed any error of law in his judgment and decree dated 9-7-2002 occasioning failure of justice.

11. Mr Shasti Sarker, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that the learned trial Court as well as the appellate Court erred in law, fact and equity in misreading of the evidence on record and in misappreciating, particularly, evidence of PWs 4 and 5 thereby arrived at wrong conclusion that the brotherhood of Haji Gandu Kha Bepari and Haji Mia Kha was not proved. He further submits that the learned Court below erred in law and facts in misconstruing the evidence on record in asmuch as, the plaintiff by adducing witnesses PW 1 to PW 5 clearly proved the plaint case; that the suit pond was the ejmali property of plaintiffs and the defendant Nos. 1 to 8 as the successors of Haji Miah Kha; that the record of the suit pond in the name of Haji Mia Kha in CS, SA and RS khatian was clearly wrong and that the learned Courts below committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

12. Mr MA Halim, the learned Advocate for the defendants-respondents-opposite parties, submits that the plaintiffs-petitioners have no right, title and possession in the suit pond; that Haji Ghandu Khan Bepari and Haji Miah Kha were not brothers of each other; that the CS record in the name of Haji Mia Kha was correctly prepared; that on the death of Haji Mia Kha his heirs executed a registered solenama on 27-8-1916 and on the basis of the solenama suit pond fell in the saharn of his son Md Yasin Khan, that Md Yasin Khan died leaving behind Abdul Mazid Kha, Abdul Mannaf Kha, Abdur Rashid Kha; that the father of the defendant Nos. 1 to 8 Md Hanif purchased the suit pond on 29-5-1973 by registered deed No. 13424 from Abdul Mannaf Khan, Nazir Ahmed Khan and Abdul Hamid Khan and later on 16-4-1980 also purchased the share of Abdul Mazid Kha through registered deed No. 8112 dated 16-4-1980 and that the name of Md Hanif was mutated; that defendant Nos. 1 to 8 have been possessing the suit pond by paying rents and that the plaintiffs brought the suit on false claims and they have no title and possession of the suit land.

13. In the face of arguments advanced by the learned Advocates of contending parties, it is necessary for us to scrutinise the material evidence on record to come to a proper decision in this case.

14. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has placed before us the plaint, the written statement, the evidence of witnesses examined by the contending parties, the material exhibits as well as the impugned judgments.

15. It is not disputed that the suit pond measuring 0.62 acres appertaining to CS plot No. 36 of CS Khatian No. 13 under Mandail Mouza of Keranigonj PS in the District of Dhaka. There is no denying of the fact that CS Khatian No. 13 was recorded in the name of Haji Mia Kha, son of Late Palton Kha Bepari, that SA record was prepared in the name of Majid Kha and Abdul Mannaf Kha, son of Md Yasin Kha, Nazir Ahmed Kha and Abdul Hamid, son of Abdul Rashid and that the suit plot was mutated in the name of Md Hanif Miah, son of late Abdul Malek Miah and who also paid rent to the government.

16. The case of the plaintiffs is that Hazi Gandu Kha took lease of 0.62 acres of land from suit plot in 1310 in the names of his 2(two) sons namely, Abdul Khaleque and Abdul Malek, but there is no document in support of their contention and no record was prepared on the basis of alleged settlement. It transpires that CS record was prepared in the name of Haji Mia Kha. Thereafter, the plaintiff has taken different view that Haji Gandu Khan and Miah Kha are full brothers and that Haji Mia Kha being eldest brother collusively prepared CS record in his name, in spite of such wrong record the heirs of Gandu Kha have been retaining title and possession in the suit pond and that on 1-1-1993 when defendant Nos. 1 to 8 in collusion with defendant No. 14 threatened the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs, then they filed suit for declaration in respect of the suit pond and for permanent injunction restraining defendant Nos. 1 to 12 from enjoying the suit pond and for declaring the SA. Khatian fraudulent and collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

17. The defence case, on the other hand, is that Haji Mia Kha, son of Palton Kha, had been possessing the suit pond by virtue of Settlement and thus CS khatian was correctly prepared in his name which is marked Exhibit 'Ka'. Haji Mia Kha transferred the suit plot to some of his heirs by different Heba Deeds but subsequently, dispute arose among the heirs of Haji Mia Kha which was resolved by a registered sole-deed dated 27-8-1996 which is marked Exhibit 'X' and as per the terms of solenama the suit plot was devolved upon Yasin Kha who died leaving 4 (four) sons namely, Mojid Kha, Abdul Mannan Kha, Abdur Rashid Kha and Roshid and 2 (two) daughters named Kameronnessa and Ameronnessa and widow Moriom Bibi. After the death of Morion Bibi, Ameronnessa and Rashid Kha, Majid Kha and Monnaf Kha, sons of Yasin, Nazir Ahmed Kha and Hamid Kha, son of Rashid Kha got the suit land by way of inheritance and by virtue of registered kabala deed dated 7-5-1973 marked exhibit 'Gha' and thus the SA record was prepared in the names of Abdul Majid Kha, Abdul Mannaf Kha, Nazir Ahmed Kha and Abdul Hamid Kha in equal share and SA record is marked exhibit Ka(1). It transpires that Abdul Majid and others paid rent to the government by rent receipts marked exhibit 'Ga' and it further transpires that father of defendant Nos. 1 to 8 Md Hanif purchased the suit pond from Mannaf Kha, Nazir Ahmed Kha, Abdul Rashid Kha and Abdul Hamid Kha by virtue of Kabala deed No. 13424 executed on 7-5-1973 marked exhibit 'Gha' and Md Hanif Miah also purchased the share of Abdul Mazid Kha by a registered Kabala No. 8112. Thus, Md Hanif Miah acquiring title of the suit land had been possessing suit land paying rent to the government by a rent receipt marked exhibit 'Ga'/1 and RS Khatian is marked Exhibit Ka /2 was prepared in his name and his name was mutated and the mutation khatian is marked exhibit 'kha'. After the death of Md Hanif Miah, his heirs, defendant Nos. 1 to 8, have been possessing the suit pond.

18. The plaintiffs failing to establish their title in the suit pond, tried to take another plea that Haji Gandu Kha Bepari, predecessors of the plaintiffs, was the brother of Haji Miah Kha who being elder brother and Karojokarok of Haji Gandu Kha Bepari illegally managed to prepare CS record in his name depriving Haji Gandu Bepari and thus the plaintiffs claim title in the suit pond by inheritance.

19. The defendant Nos. 1 to 8 vehemently opposed such assertion of the plaintiffs. The defence case is that Haji Mia Kha was the son of Late Palton Kha of village Amirabagh, whereas Haji Gandu Kha was the son of Late Ashraf Bepari of village Kusiararbagh.

20. CS Khatian proves that father's name of Haji Miah Kha was Paltan Kha but plaintiffs without filing any document failed to prove that Gandu Kha's father's name was also Paltan Kha. The plaintiff No. 1 as PW 1 admitted in his evidence that Mia Kha hails from village Amirabagh and that the village of Gandu Kha is at Kusiarbagh. PW 2 Basu Mia knows nothing about the relationship of Gandu Mia Kha and Miah Kha. PW 5 deposed that he has no document to show that Haji Gandu Kha and Mia Kha are full brothers. PW 3 Ishaque Mia deposed nothing on this point. PW 4 Aynal Hoque deposed that he has nothing to show that Gandhu Kha and Miah Kha are brothers.

21. On the other hand, defendant No. 3 as DW 1 deposed that there was no relationship between Hazi Gandu Kha and Haji Mia Kha, DW 2 Md Yakob categorically deposed that Haji Mia Kha was son of Paltan Kha whereas Gandu Kha was the son of Ashraf Bepari.

22. The plaintiffs-appellants-petitioners filed suit for declaration of title and for permanent injunction. In such case burden of proof lies on the person who desires any court to give judgment as to any legal right. Section 101 of the Evidence Act runs thus:

"Whoever desires any court to give judgment as of any legal right or liability dependent on the existence of facts which he asserts must prove that those facts exist. When a person is bound to prove the existence of any fact, it is said that the burden of proof lies on that person."

<u>23. The burden of proof lies on the party who substantially asserts the affirmative of the issue and not upon the party who denies it. It is reasonable and just that the suitor who relies upon the existence of a fact should be called upon to prove his own case. The party on whom the onus of proof lies must, in order to succeed, establish the case. He cannot, on failure to do so, take advantage of the weakness of his adversary's case. He must succeed by the strength of his own right and the clearness of his own proof. The burden of proving the case is upon the claimant.</u>

24. In the instant case, the plaintiffs claim their title on two counts, firstly, they claim that Haji Gandu Kha took lease of 0.62 acres of land in the names of his sons Abdul Khaleque and Abdul Alek and the subsequent heirs of Abdul Khaleque and Abdul Malek, who are plaintiffs, claim the suit land by virtue of lease. But the plaintiffs have totally failed to file any documents of lessee or any records of the alleged lease and secondly, the plaintiffs claim that Gandu Kha was the full brother of recorded tenant Haji Mia Kha and thus the successors of Gandu Kha who are plaintiffs, acquired the suit land by inheritance and thus they are in joint possession of the successors of Mia Kha. The brotherly relationship of Gandu Kha and Mia Kha has not been proved nor has been proved any benami transaction by Mia Kha and thus successors plaintiffs of Gandu Kha acquired nothing from Mia Kha and their possession in the suit land has not also been proved.

<u>25. Since the plaintiffs have failed to prove the title and possession in the suit land, as such, their prayer for injunction does not lie. We find support of this view by the rulings reported in 14 DLR 44 and 22 DLR 385.</u>

<u>26. Section 110 of the Evidence Act gives effect to the principle that possession is prima facie evidence of complete title; anyone who intends to oust the possessor must establish a right to do so. This is to be presumed from lawful possession until the want of title or a better title is proved. Possession is prima facie proof of ownership, possession has a two-fold value; it is the evidence of ownership, and is itself the foundation of a right to possession.</u>

<u>27. In the instant case, the plaintiffs claim title along with the contesting defendants and such assertion of the plaintiffs' possession in the suit land have not at all been proved. On the other hand, the title and possession of the contesting defendants on the basis of valid deed has been proved. The defendants possession in the suit land has strengthened the title of the defendants in the suit land.</u>

28. By section 101 of the Evidence Act, the plaintiff has to prove the whole of the facts which he alleges to entitle him to judgment.

29. But section 103 of the Evidence Act states that "The burden of proof as to any particular fact lies on that person who wishes the court to believe in its existence, unless it is provided by any law that the proof of that fact shall lie on any particular person." when the defendant alleges that he has right, title and interest in the suit property which the plaintiff does not accept. In such circumstances it be Comes a fact which is asserted by the defendant and is denied by the plaintiff. As per section 103 of the Evidence Act, the onus of proving the same is on the defendant. Whenever a person asserts affirmatively as part of his case that a certain state of things is present or is absent, or that a particular thing is insufficient for a particular purpose, that is an averment which he is bound to prove affirmatively.

<u>30. Here, in this case, the plaintiffs claim the suit pond firstly by way of lease and alternatively by inheritance showing Gandu Kha as full brother of Mia Kha and both the assertions of the plaintiffs have been proved false. When the assertions of the plaintiffs have not been proved, than as per provision of section 103 of the Evidence Act, the burden rebuts to the defendants. Then we have to see how far the assertions of defendants have been proved. It appears from the evidence on record that the predecessors of the defendant Haji Mia Kha claimed title in suit pond by way of settlement and accordingly, CS record was prepared in the name of Mia Kha, that the heirs of Mia Kha transferred the suit pond to Abdul Mannaf Kha and others and on the basis of this sale deed, SA record was prepared in the name of Abdul Mannaf, Abdul Majid, Nazir Ahmed and Abdul Hamid and the Khatian market Exhibit Ka(1) who also paid rent through rent receipt marked Exhibit 'Ga'. It further transpires from evidence that Abdul Mannaf and others having right, title, interest and possession in the suit pond transferred the same in favour of Md Hanif Mia by a kabala deed No. 13424 dated 7-5-1993 marked exhibit-Gha who also mutated his name through mutation khatian marked Exhibit Kha(2) and Hanif Miah also paid rent by rent receipt marked Exhibit Ga(1). Thus the assertion of the defendants to the effect that they have title and possession in the suit pond has been proved.</u>

31. It is well settled principle of law that the plaintiff is to prove its case which the plaintiffs of this case have totally failed. On the other hand, the defendants have proved their assertion.

32. A plaintiff in order to get declaration in respect of any land, he must have 'legal character' to institute the suit against any person and such character is envisaged in section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act runs thus:

"Any person entitled to any legal character, or to any right as to any property, may institute a suit against any person denying, or interested to deny, his title to such character or right, and the court may, in its discretion, make therein a declaration that he is so entitled, and the plaintiff need not in such suit ask for any further relief.

Provided that no court shall make any such declaration where the plaintiff, being able to seek further relief than a mere declaration of title, omits to do so."

33. The object of this section is merely to perpetuate and strengthen testimony regarding title of the plaintiff so that adverse attacks on it may not weaken it. This section does not sanction any and every kind of declaration but only a declaration that the plaintiff is entitled to a specific legal character or to any right as to property.

34. Legal character has been taken to mean legal status. Legal character is meant status or the position which a person occupies in the eye of law. Duties and functions of the courts are to decide disputes between parties in accordance with law.

35. The relief claimed under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act is, no doubt, discretionary, but the real test for its application is, whether the plaintiff recalling apprehends that an interested person may deny the plaintiff's title. The jurisdiction to give a declaratory judgment should be exercised sparingly with great care and with extreme caution. The relief being discretionary no person can claim declaration as of right. The court has discretion to grant it or not on consideration of all circumstances of the case and evidence on record. Though the grant of a declaratory relief is entirely at the discretion of the court, the discretion has to be exercised on certain well recognised principles. That is the plaintiff has to prove its case to the hilt and a declaration cannot be given whose conduct is fraudulent. Where a declaratory decree has been given by the trial Court, the appellate Court or the Court of revision should not interfere unless it is satisfied that the lower Court acted in an arbitrary or perverse manner. These courts would however, not intervene when the Court of first instance had soundly exercised its discretion.

<u>36. In the instant case, on perusal of the evidence on record, it appears the plaintiffs have totally failed to prove their case by oral and documentary evidence. Their contention of lease has no legs to stand which is totally false. Moreover, the plaintiffs have not come to the court with clean hands to get a discretionary relief as the plaintiffs tried to show his predecessor Gandu Kha as the brother of Mia Kha which has been proved false and fraudulent. Sections 42 and 56 of the Specific Relief Act deal respectively with suits for declaration and injunction, both being discretionary and equitable reliefs which the plaintiffs of this case have sought for. The principle laid down in section 56(J) rests on the maximum that he who seeks equity must do equity and should come with clean hands. In this case, the plaintiffs have totally failed to prove their case. Moreover, they have not come to the court with clean hands, so they cannot get equity.</u>

37. The learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of the evidence on record dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 9-7-2000. On appeal, the learned Additional District Judge also dismissed the appeal by the judgment dated 20-5-2002 affirming the judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge. The learned Subordinate Judge framing the issues elaborately discussed each point separately giving reasons thereon and his judgment does not suffer any legal infirmity, rather his judgment is self-contained and well-reasoned. The learned Additional District Judge passed his judgment disclosing the points of determination on proper appreciation of the evidence on record. Our Appellate Division in the case of Abdul Matin Choudhury vs Chapala Rani Sen and others reported in 37 DLR (AD) 205 held that concurrent findings of facts by the trial Court and the first appellate Court is binding upon the High Court Division unless it could be shown that the said finding had been vitiated by an error of law or of procedure which has affected the merit of the case. We find that the judgment of the trial Court as well as of the appellate Court committed no error of law or of principle which has not affected the merit of the case and the judgment of the trial Court as well as of the appellate Court deserve consideration.

39. In view of what we have discussed and considered above, we are of the opinion that the learned Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka committed no error of law in an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned judgment affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

40. We, therefore, find no merit in the revision which fails accordingly.

41. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree affirming the judgment of the trial Court are upheld.

Send down the LCR at once.

End.
